utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. May I remind you, sir, of the affirmation which still applies as you give your evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. M-088. If you remember, we spoke yesterday about the fact that on the 10th of August, 2001, you were with your truck at the border crossing of the Stenkovac. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you explained it yesterday, this border crossing is not far away from the border crossing of Blace. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that border crossing is more or less seven to eight kilometres away from Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many kilometres it's away from Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask, Your Honours, to move into a private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You testified that you were informed by telephone about the mine incident in Ljubotenski Bacila; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed, I learned it from my cousin that there was a problem in Ljuboten, but I didn't know exactly what the problem was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You decided to return to the village immediately; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You left the truck at the border crossing, and together with your (redacted), you went back to the village. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First I went to Skopje and then back to the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And from the border crossing of Stenkovac, you were not able to see anything happening above your village on -- in the Basineci area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were not able to see that because of the distance or because you were really not able to observe that area from Stenkovci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you just said, first you went to Skopje, you took a taxi, and together with your relative you came to Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone were to claim that you arrived to Skopje with a private vehicle, that statement would not be correct; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please? I wasn't clear about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone were to claim that you did not came by taxi but with a private vehicle, then the person claiming that would not be speaking the truth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the border, from Blace to Skopje, there are private cars, taxis.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But those private cars did not belong neither to you nor to your relative; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As a truck driver, you never had any problems with the police before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any problems with the police in the city, but I did have a problem with the police at the check-point at the exit of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the same company, you went from Skopje to the bus-stop in Radisani; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not continue going by bus, but you decided to go to the village on foot through the fields?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Up to the bus station of Radishan, I don't remember how I went there. But from there, we walked back to Ljuboten through the fields.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You used the shortcut through the fields so to escape meeting the police or to avoid meeting other persons that might be on that path; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But usually you did not go to the village through the fields?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I [Realtime transcript read in error "don't know"] didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Once you arrived in Ljuboten, together with the person that you came with --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. In line 7, I think the answer have been entered incorrectly, because I asked the witness whether he usually used the road through the villages. He said, No, I didn't, and then here it is written, No, I don't know. Maybe I should repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that usually you didn't go to the village through the fields?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually I took the road. It was only that day that I walked through the fields.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I -- what I understood you. So once you arrived in the village, together with the person that you arrived with, you went to the premises of the crisis committee; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First I went home, and then later I went to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the premises of the Crisis Staff, there were also other persons from Ljuboten to come to an agreement what to do and how to organise the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct that there were other villagers, but they were discussing how to pull out of the village, the civilians and their families, what to do with the families, with their own families.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in addition to you and the person that you arrived with in -- to the village, that Afet Zendeli was also in the meeting together with Hisni Murseli, Fatmir Kamberi, Kenan Salievski, the brother of Fatmir Kamberi, Rami Jusufi, Baki Halimi, Adem Murseli, and also other persons from the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember who was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you surely remember that there was a large -- a large number of people present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that there were many people there, but at this moment I don't recall who actually was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Is that correct that various opinions were presented at the meeting? Some thought that that should give resistance if someone would enter the village, while the others thought that they should leave the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't hear many things because I stayed there for a short while, and I went back to the family. I can't tell you what they talked about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the meeting there were discussions about the mine incident, and you learned that several members of the army have been killed and that two of the persons killed are from the neighbouring village of Ljubanci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything about that. I didn't hear anything about people being killed or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I may suggest, or ask you to recall, that during the meeting, there were discussions that several armed persons have entered the village on that day, among whom was Sheravin [as interpreted] Bajrami. Is that information that you got?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not true. I didn't hear anything about that and there wasn't any armed person in Ljuboten. There were only innocent civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Quite a while before this event, the Crisis Staff of the village organised some guards at the entrance of the village so they would be able to control who is entering the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You knew that there is a real threat that the security forces might search the village, because at that time a significant number of young people from the village was actively participating in the NLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was simply a driver, and I was working very hard. I stayed at home only one day every week, so I can't say that there were a large number of armed people in the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say that at that time, the members of NLA from the village were among the others Rasim Murati, Faik Murati, Shefajet Bajrami, Besim Murtezani, Jetulla Arifi, Bekri Ajdini, Orhan Bajrami, Shefket Murati -- Shefket Murati, correction, Refedin Selimi, and Feriz Selimi, you could confirm this as being true. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may say for some but not for everyone, because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As the -- as my learned colleague the Prosecutor asked you, you have given statements to the investigator of the OTP in the past, and then you spoke about everything that was known to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask now that the witness is shown his statement, which is 65 ter number 1D84, page 1D1146.12; and the Albanian version, page 1D1160.12. I think the document got the number P206 yesterday, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask ... I will ask you to have a look at .12 of your statement. In the middle, you say: "I think that around 20 persons from Ljuboten belonged to the NLA. Being asked if I know the persons Riza Jonuzi, Rasim Murati, Faik Murati, Shefajet Bajrami, Besim Murtezani, Jetulla Arifi, Bekri Ajdini, Orhan Bajrami, Shefket Murati, Refedin Selimi, Feriz Selimi, Suat Saliu, Rafiz Bajrami, I confirm that I know these persons. Most of them belong to the NLA ..." I can't say who they were but, "for example, Saud Saliu and Riza Jonuzi are police officers." Is that what you said at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said so, but I also said that I can't confirm that every one of them was NLA member, and this is how it's written here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your explanation. Tell me, is it true that because of the situation which was the cause of the meeting of the Crisis Staff and because of the fear that the village might be searched, already on August 10, around 40 to 50 families fled the village and went towards Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What does "no" mean? That the families did not go to Skopje; or that you don't know? What were you trying to answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to say that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true if I were to say that an agreement was reached at the meeting to organise checkpoints out of whom one would be located next to the house of Qani Jashari?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters comment: We didn't hear the name well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, it's well written. Tell me, are you aware that one of the checkpoints was supposed to be next to the -- Qani Jashari's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I didn't hear anything. I told you earlier that I stayed there only for a brief time, and I returned to my family. So I have no information about what they talked.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And on Sunday, 12th of August, could you confirm that from that point, from the area of Qani Jashari's house, there was shooting towards the positions of the army and the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. There wasn't any firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Qani Jashari's house in Ljuboten is located in such a -- such an area that both the house and the tobacco field, as well as the field towards the woods, could be well observed from the positions of the Macedonian Army that were located directly above the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't say that, because I was never in that house, and as I told you, I stayed only for some five minutes, and I can't say whether you can see something from that place.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was not what could be observed from the place of Qani Jashari's house, but, rather, once goes up the hill just beyond the village at which army positions were, the positions of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, because I presume in peacetime you had had an opportunity to climb up there. Therefore, my question is: Is it correct that from that position, one can see the area around Qani Jashari's house as well as a meadow nearby, through which one would move from his house towards the nearby forested area and the mountains?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The house is in a depression, so you cannot see from there. But from the place where they grow tobacco, I think you can see that place from the mountain, Stena Mountain.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we move briefly into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness M-088, is it correct that you did not see the person who joined you being wounded, shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I did not understand your question. Could you ask it again, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While running, you did not see how it came about that that person was wounded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only learned that he had been wounded when he came to the woods. I saw that he had been wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also did not see how and when Bajram -- or, rather, Kadri Jashari and Xhelal Bajrami were hit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because everybody else was behind me. I was the first to run and reach the woods. I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know and were not told from which exact position the bullet that had struck the wounded person came from, and the same applies to Xhelal Bajrami and Kadri Jashari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bullets were coming from the left, from Malistena, but also from behind where the forces were stationed on the road in front of Qani Jashari's house. I mean, the Macedonian police were stationed there. So the bullets were coming from the left and from behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But you don't know from which positions the bullets that hit those men were fired from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you stopped in the woods, you turned back towards the village, and as you testified at that moment you saw that Qani Jashari's house was ablaze; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were able to go to that house, you were probably able to notice that there was a haystack immediately nearby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were in the house, neither the haystack nor the house itself were on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the moment I was there, the house was not on fire; that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also did not see who or how set the house on fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Because I only saw the fire when I arrived at the woods. I could see the roof on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also testified that after those events, you took active participation with the NLA. You became a member of the 314th Brigade of the NLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After these events, you never reported any of it to the police, and you have never given any statements to the Macedonian authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I did not give any statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You provided your statements to investigators of the International Tribunal, and you believed it to be sufficient to help in discovering potential perpetrators; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have no knowledge of anyone else from the village having gone to the police, or to the prosecutor's office, or to any of the courts in order to report any events or report on any persons about whom you testified today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try and put it another way. Do you know whether anyone submitted a claim or a report of such nature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A correction for the transcript because I misspoke when I referred to the brigade number. It is stated that it was 314th, which is indeed what I said. Instead it should have been the 114th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also -- you also know that in April 2002, when there was an exhumation of the deceased, no uniformed police presence was allowed at the site of the exhumation; the Macedonian police, that is. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not. I -- I'm not aware whether the police was there or not. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my colleague Jasmina Zivkovic will be cross-examining the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness M-088, good afternoon to you, too. My name is Jasmina Zivkovic and together with my learned friend Antonio Apostolski, I appear on behalf of Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Witness M-088, we heard from my learned friend Ms. Residovic some basic information about you; for example, where and when you were born and what is your level of education. Nowadays, you live together with your family; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You also told us that during the Ljuboten events, you were employed as a driver. Can you tell us what is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now I work as a farmer and I also sell my produce. So I also trade a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In August 2001, during the Ljuboten events, you still resided with your parents in the same house, and you had no family of your own; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I was living with my family.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Today, you confirmed to my learned friend that on Friday, the 10th of August, you were in Stenkovac with Zemri Zendeli, and you left your truck there, after which you took a taxi to Skopje. You claim that throughout that period, you were with Zemri Zendeli. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that from Radishan to Ljuboten, you went on foot through the fields. Can you tell us whether there was any particular reason for you to go on foot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason was because I didn't want to go through the police checkpoint, which is at the exit of Ljuboten village on the road towards Skopje. I didn't want to be ill-treated, and that's why I didn't follow the main road that goes to Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that you were afraid of the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was afraid because I had suffered ill-treatment at this checkpoint before. For example, when I went to the city once, I was ill-treated there. They took my identity card and kept me for half an hour there without giving me any reason why they were detaining me for that time. That's why I didn't want to go through the check-point.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Was that during the events when there were quite a -- quite a number of terrorist actions going on in the neighbouring villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened after the establishment of the police check-points. I don't recall when it was, one or two months before what happened. And this happened when I went to work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Once you arrived in Ljuboten around noon, you went to your house where you stayed with your family in the basement until the Saturday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what is correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that -- the truth is that I went home to my family, and then I went to the Crisis Staff for a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On Saturday, you were in the house for the entire day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And because of that, you were not able to see what was going on in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that on Sunday, August 12th, the shelling started at around 8.00 in the morning and that around 10.00, together with Zemri Zendeli, you went to Afet Zendeli's house. Could you tell us how long did you stay in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may say that I stayed there for a short period of time. I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You also said today that -- to my learned colleague Ms. Residovic, that at that moment there were 30 people in that house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: After that, you, together with Zemri Zendeli, went to Zendel Zendeli's house, since in Afet Zendeli's house you did not feel very safe anymore; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went in the direction of Zendel Zendeli's house to leave for the forest because this is where his house is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether you understood what I said. My question was: Why did you leave Zendel Zendeli's house? Is that because you didn't feel safe there anymore?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left Afet Zendeli's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I apologise, that's my mistake; we're talking about Afet Zendeli's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that the remaining 28 people felt -- continued to feel safe in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't feel safe either.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Once you entered Qani Jashari's house, you immediately went to the room at the back, and you only stayed in the house for five minutes, and during that five minutes you were all together; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: From that room, which is on the back side of the house, you were not able to see what was going on in front of the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, I couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Once you jumped through the window, you said you hided in the tobacco field, which was next to the house, and it was there when you first find -- when you saw the Hermelin for the first time in front of the house; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, but Hermelin was on the road that leads to Rastak.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In your statements, you've said that you saw only two uniformed police officers next to the Hermelin at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct. I saw only two or three policemen close to the Hermelin.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-088, since you started running right after you saw the police officers, you weren't able to see what uniforms they wore and what kind of weapons they had on them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I started running, I didn't look back, but from the tobacco field I could see those two, three policemen that I mentioned, because there was a large noise coming from the direction, meaning there was a greater number of policemen, but I saw only two or three policemen in uniforms in black uniforms and with masks, black masks, who had this Hermelin nearby.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask if we could move into a private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-088, if I understood you well, you said that from the tobacco field you went towards the woods, Guri i Bardhe. First you were crawling for -- for 500 metres until you reached the first bush. And that took you only a few minutes. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I said that first I ran for a while, then I crawled up to the place.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: At one point you hid into the bushes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask to have the witness shown photograph 65 ter 199.10.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-088, do you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark on this photograph --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Could you see the bushes that you hid in on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see them. But can you please repeat the question once more? Maybe I didn't get it well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You got it well, that's what I asked you, whether you see the bushes that you temporarily took shelter in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see the bushes where I hid.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So could you tell us where these bushes are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are in this direction, in the direction of the forest. You can't see them in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, could you tell us how high this bush was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were small bushes in an open field. I wouldn't say they were high or tall like a forest is. Simply small bushes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. M-088, you said you didn't see what was going on with the other persons -- persons behind you. You also stated that you only heard fires -- shots being fired behind you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that it might be possible that Kadri Jashari, Bajram Jashari, and Xhelal Bajrami could have fired at the Macedonian security forces without you knowing that, since you didn't see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. This is not true. It cannot be true, because they too had fled the house up to the tobacco field. Until that moment, they didn't have any weapons on them, so you might ask with what would they be firing, if they did fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you left Zemri Zendeli with a -- with a shepherd in the forest and you continued to the Matejce monastery; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I left Zemri on the 14th of August, 2001 in -- when I arrived Kumanov, I didn't leave Zemri in the mountain near Ljuboten but in Kumanov.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You were in the Matejce monastery after you've ran into the forest; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After I went to the forest, then I went to Matejce monastery to ask for assistance (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thanks. Did you become a NLA member in Matejce?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-088, on the occasion when you enrolled into the NLA, did you give an oath?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because there was an agreement already signed at that time. I simply put on a uniform but didn't do anything, wasn't given any task.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So you joined the NLA after the framework agreement was signed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, why did you join?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I wanted to take (redacted) up to that zone or to some other place because he was wounded and I had to go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You surely knew what the purposes or the goals of the NLA were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the NLA -- the NLA was fighting -- was fighting for territory in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know maybe whether the end goal of the NLA was to take apart the territories that were one, to secede them and join them to Kosovo and Albania, in order to create greater Albania?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I think that the transcript misses the words "secede from the Republic of Macedonia."

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood your question, but I have no answer to give you because this is a matter I have no information about. You might ask some person who is more learned than I or who has been dealing with such issues. I am not in a position to give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: That means that you surely do not know why the -- what the NLA was fighting for; is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The NLA was fighting for the rights pertaining to a citizen or a resident or inhabitant of that state. They simply fought for their rights.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean the rights of the Albanians when you say so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-088, were you educated in your native Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I learned Albanian until I finished the primary, the 8th year school. Then for three other years, I learned in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So you finished elementary education in your native language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to vote freely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I think this is an irrelevant question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have members of parliament that were of Albanian ethnicity who were elected in free elections in the parliament in 2002, in Macedonia -- I apologise, in 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were Albanians who were elected.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have ministers in the government that were of Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember for the moment. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember maybe that the minister of justice at the time was an Albanian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-088, we will go back a little bit to the questions related to the events? Do you remember, since you were all the time together with Zemri Zendeli, whether -- or maybe you were in contact with his brother Islam during the Ljuboten event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this. I don't know this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Does it mean you weren't in contact with him at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to either you or Zemri Zendeli, were any of you -- any -- were there any of you were in contact with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. We didn't have any contacts.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So that might mean that he might have been with the NLA at that time without you knowing it, since you had no contacts with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He lived in Skopje and I was doing my job, so I had no information as to his whereabouts at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that Suad Saliu and Riza Jonuzi were NLA members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember for the moment, but Idriz Jonuzi I don't think this is the right name.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Riza Jonuzi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that he was. I don't remember for the moment whether he was or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that they were police officers during the Ljuboten events, between 10 and 12 August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When I gave the statement, I thought that they were policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So you remember saying that in your statement, that they were policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. But this is what I thought for that moment, because after 2001 they were policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, given the time maybe it will be good to go for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you want to tender the photograph that you had the witness mark?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's not necessary because he didn't mark the bushes, so it is not necessary, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we will be losing that image. We will adjourn now and resume at 20 past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness M-088, concerning some people whose names were put forth by my learned friend Ms. Residovic, you confirmed for them that they were NLA members. However, you said that you cannot be certain for all of them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, concerning some of those people for whom you've confirmed they were members of the NLA, did you see any of them after having reached the Matejce monastery where the NLA was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I arrived there, I felt very tired, and maybe I saw some of them, but I felt very weak and tired.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you speak to any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember to have spoken to any one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that those people opened fire at members of the Macedonian forces from the direction of Pop Cesme?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that Islam Zendeli, that you didn't see him at Ljuboten. Did you see him perhaps at the Matejce monastery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Zemri Zendeli was in a hospital. First, he went to Lipkovo and then in Nikustak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they sent him to a place, I think to Lipkov, but as to where he was, this I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: It means that during the month of him being hospitalised, you didn't pay him a visit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. I was about two weeks, I think, or ten days a member of NLA. Then I left Matejce in the direction of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness M-088, does the name of Xhezair Shaqiri mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: While you were at the Matejce monastery, did you on that occasion see any NLA wounded soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of Baki Halimi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. No. That person, Baki Halimi, is a teacher from Ljuboten village, and I know him simply as a teacher who used to be my teacher up to the 8th grade. He taught me history and geography.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that you don't know that he also participated in the fights with the Macedonian forces at Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't take part in any fight against the Macedonian forces. No one from Ljuboten did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At Matejce, there is a monastery several centuries old. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know how old the monastery is, or are you not familiar with the fact that there is a monastery there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there is a monastery there, but how old that monastery is, this I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Is it a Christian monastery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, because I never saw it before.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: During your stay in Matejce, were you able to notice that the entire monastery was demolished?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot say that it was demolished. I told you that I stayed there only for a while, and I didn't see that it was demolished.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, indeed. Ms. Regue, is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Witness, my learned colleague Ms. Residovic in page 11, line 19, asked you whether you became a member of the 114th Brigade of the NLA and you answered that was correct. Ms. Zivkovic, in page 30, line 24, you answer actually to her question that you were a member of the NLA in Matejce for ten days, two weeks, and then you went to Kosovo. During that time, did you participate in any sort of training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you participate in any sort of military operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two months.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Where did you go afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Kosova, I returned home to my family.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic also asked you in page 16, line 23, whether you had ever given any statement to the Macedonian authorities, and you said that you didn't. Why you didn't give any statement to Macedonian authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't for reasons of personal safety.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please elaborate a bit about this point, "personal safety"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By this, I want to say that I was afraid of the Macedonian police. I didn't feel secure in their presence.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Were you ever contacted by any Macedonian authority who inquire you about the events in Ljuboten, the weekend of 10 to 12th August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could I please display in e-court system P206, please? It's the witness's statement. And if we could show paragraph 25? Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: My learned colleague Ms. Zivkovic read to you a line from the paragraph 25, which is: "I can't even tell whether the uniforms were camouflage." But she means the next line, actually, which is: "To me, it was a sort of police uniform, dark in colour." Do you agree with the complete sentence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you clarify one matter for the Chamber? After you had been at the position of the monastery for some ten days or two weeks, you went to Kosovo. I think you indicated you were there for about two months. What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed there as a guest, as someone who wanted to spend some time. I stayed there until I felt stronger and then I returned home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Of whom were you a guest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the 2001 conflict, I had some refugees from Viti in Kosova staying with my family. So when I went to Kosova, I stayed with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You stayed all the time with a family that you knew; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When you left the monastery, did you obtain permission from anybody to leave, to go to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the soldiers who were at the monastery had permission. There was a commander whose pseudonym was Paloshi, and then we left for Kosova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did everybody leave for Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may say that all, but I can't be very sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did the commander leave with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you stay with any NLA people when you were in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-088 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was the only one staying with that family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's unlikely, but is there anything arising from that that either Defence feels they need to pursue? I see no being nodded by both counsel. Ms. Regue? Thank you. You will be pleased to know that that concludes your questioning. The Chamber thanks you for your attendance here in the The Hague and for the assistance that you have been able to give, and you are now able to return to your family, and we thank you indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This may be a convenient time to deal with what I understand is a matter or one or two matters that you wish to raise, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Since the beginning of our court session today, the number of matters has risen from two to three. I will try to deal with them as expeditiously as I can. First of all, there is a witness who we would expect to begin testifying at some point tomorrow. May we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm referring to the Witness M-21 that you contemplate calling Friday. The Chamber remains surprised that you continued to anticipate two hours for the witness. I think I suggested the other day it is more probably two days. And unless you know something remarkable that we do not, I find it difficult to think that that witness can be concluded in the space of just two hours. But more to the point concerning him is a motion which I received today to actually admit his Rule 92 ter statement with addendum. Could the Chamber make clear that we are not and have not admitted any statements under Rule 92 bis or 92 ter until the witness is here in Court. In the case of Rule 92 bis, and there remains some witnesses who as are within the realm of 92 bis, there must then be compliance with the form required by the rule of the statement before it is admitted, and the final decision on its relevance will depend on the state of the evidence at that point. With respect to 92 ter, the statement simply cannot be admitted until the witness here on oath accepts and verifies the statement as the evidence the witness would give. So that we can't admit it at this point, and certainly the addendum is something which will of necessity be referred to by the witness as we anticipate it, because it is expected that the witness will say with the corrections, additions or deletions set out in the addendum, the statement is the evidence that I would give. So that if that is what comes to transpire, the time then will be for the Chamber to admit the statement, subject, of course, to any objection that might be raised. For that reason, can we say that the Chamber will certainly not be dealing with the written motion that has been received and neither Defence needs to prepare any response to it. If there is any objection, it will be dealt with orally when the witness is here, not that we anticipate that there would be. Is that clear enough, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is very clear and if the Prosecution has created any confusion, then it is my fault and I apologise for that. I would like, with your leave, to explain why the Prosecution has filed what it has. We have filed this statement, the statement of M-21, I believe, pursuant to the order/decision of the Trial Chamber, that after such consolidated statements are created pursuant to Rule 92 ter, they must be disclosed to the Defence, and I believe the term used by the Trial Chamber in their decision was "submit." And perhaps that's where I made an error by titling this submission as motion. And, if so, we did not mean to suggest in any way that the Chamber would deal with this before the witness was present in the courtroom. And we will, if necessary, in the future refrain from referring to such submissions as motions. Your Honour, with respect to the time that Witness M-021 may take, again I regret if I misunderstood your comments from last week. I understood your comments from last week to mean that the Prosecution had underestimated the time that this witness would -- would take during his testimony here. And the Prosecution does not disagree with Your Honour's comment. It is my understanding that if we get to Witness M-21 beginning on Friday, the witness's evidence would begin, and we would advance to a particular position that we needed to until a quarter to 2.00, and then that witness would probably have to return at a later date to finish the witness's testimony. I did not mean to suggest that we would finish with the witness on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. But the Chamber would encourage you in the course of the Prosecution case, as it will other counsel if there are Defence cases to be pursued, to make realistic assessments of the length of time that will be needed for a witness, and I think that is a starkly unrealistic assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that then. Is it practical now to call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And Ms. Motoike will lead the next witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, good afternoon. At this time, the Prosecution would call Witness M-092. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the sheet of paper handed to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think Ms. Motoike has some questions for you now. She is over here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. And could I please have the usher's assistance in providing the witness with a document that bears ERN number 04247862 -- 04247862.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, can you please take a look at this piece of paper that's in front of you and tell us - without reading it aloud - whether the information contained on that piece of paper is true and correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, after my learned colleagues have had a chance to see this, and there is no objection, I would ask to tender it under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P214, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you have been granted protective measures of face and voice distortion in this case, and therefore, your face and your voice will be distorted to the public, and we will also be referring to you as witness or Witness M-092. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall giving a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on 10 June 2004?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall, in August 2006, that this statement was certified by an officer of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And at that time, did you have an opportunity to read the statement in your native language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity to make corrections and/or additions to that statement in August of 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes. Because of some technical mistakes that were found there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And were some of these corrections and/or additions handwritten into your statement and also encompassed in an addenda -- addendum to your statement at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Some of them were written remarks. Yes, they were like this, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And were the contents of your statements, with the corrections and the additions, at that time true and correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes, they were correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: On 10 May 2007, did you meet with myself and another colleague here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And at that time, during that meeting, did you have an additional correction as to the name of a doctor that was indicated in your statement in paragraphs 23 and 24?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall what the correction was with respect to the name of that doctor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Ridvan Tahiraj and Ridvan Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And which is the correct name of the doctor that you refer to in those paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Ridvan Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would seek to tender the 92 bis statement, which bears ERN N002-7240 - N002-7256, under seal, pursuant to 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P215, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. And at this time, with Your Honours' permission, I would read a summary of this particular statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: "The witness observed that approximately two and a half months prior to the Ljuboten attack on 10 through 12 August 2001, there over 20 Macedonian military and police check-points around the village of Ljuboten. On 10 August 2001, Macedonian government forces launched an attack against Ljuboten which continued intermittently through August 12th. "On 12 August 2001, the witness heard screaming from the direction of the houses of Adem Ametovski and Zija Ameti. The witness saw armed Macedonian forces and a Hermelin. After the shelling commenced on 12 August 2001, the witness and others decided to leave the village. The witness and others sought shelter in the house of Qani Jashari. The witness saw no weapons or ammunition there and as the persons in this house left the house they fled across the fields and were fired upon by Macedonian forces. The witness was wounded in the leg and he also saw that Kadri Jashari had been shot. The witness observed Kadri Jashari's house burning after they fled the area that day. "The witness became a NLA member after 12 August 2001. Other Ljuboten villagers also belonged to the NLA, but they were all in Nikustak from 10 through 12 August 2001. "There was a NLA operation, according to the witness, in the mountains above Ljuboten on the afternoon of the 12 August. The NLA did not engage the Macedonian forces in Ljuboten and there were no NLA fighters in the village from 10 through 12 August 2001." If we could please pull up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do, the addendum sheet, are you tendering that as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It has the -- the addendum sheet which, I believe, is bearing ERN N0027253 through N0027256, has also been certified pursuant to 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received as part of the same exhibit as the actual statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please pull up a photograph bearing ERN N005-7603? It is also a photograph which appears on page 5 of the court binder. Could we go -- further out, zoom out, please. Zoom out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you mention shelling from an area called Malistena on Friday, 10/8/2001, in paragraph 8 of your statement, and also in paragraphs 12 and 19 of your statement, you also indicate that there's shelling and shooting coming from this area called Malistena on 12/8/2001. Do you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you please mark for us with the usher's assistance, perhaps? Well, let me ask you this: Is the area called Malistena depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you, please, mark for us the area which is referred to as Malistena?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Is it marked correctly?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: The red circle that you have marked on the photograph, is that the location that you refer to as Malistena?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yeah. I call it Malistena.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is a location -- you refer to location called Pop Cesme in paragraph 22 of your statement. Is that also -- is that area also depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: This is not depicted in that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you describe for us where the location of Pop Cesme is, in relation to Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: From Rek [phoen] is on the opposite side. It's about six kilometres or maybe seven kilometres far away from the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: When you say opposite side and you made a hand gesture, what do you mean? Where in relation to Ljuboten is it located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes. This is on the other side of Ljuboten, in the straight in the same direction with the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could use south, east, west, could you tell us in relation to Ljuboten, is it south of Ljuboten, west of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: It is more going to the east.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: East, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please tender this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P216, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we please show 65 ter 199.10, page 259?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 199.10 has only one page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Please, that page, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you describe being at the house of Qani Jashari in your statement, and at some point you indicated that you left this house from a window and ran into a field. Do you see the photo before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is that window depicted in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, Witness, could you please mark the window you ran from and perhaps label it with a number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And could you also, using the marker, mark the path that you took after leaving through this window on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you label that red line that you've made on the photograph with a number 2, please? You also mention --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You also mention in your statement that you were shot in the leg while you were in the field. Could you mark the location where this occurred, please, and label it with a number 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes. I can mark it, but it's a bit high up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Perhaps I should have asked you: Is it the location where you were wounded in the leg depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes. It is very close, indeed, it's just a bit -- five metres close, and Kadri Jashari was killed before me in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you mark for the -- with a -- could you mark then the area where you say Kadri Jashari was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes. It's a bit higher up because there were some plumb trees there and the road was a bit higher up, and I have been walking through that area, and the bullets were -- were going through over our shoulders, and then that's -- that's the path we -- we went. And when I turned towards Kadri, and then I was also wounded in my leg. And after this, I was unable to approach him more closer, but I was running quickly because I was trying to escape the bullets and the shots that were coming from many directions from down, from the side, and it is also from the place where I marked it in Malistena, because bullets were coming from everywhere. If I need to mark number 3 here, I can mark it, where I was wounded, for Kadri Jashari.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes, could you, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Number 2 and number 3. But it looks like 23, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: It does. Perhaps you could put a circle around the 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... a circle around the 2. So that's the point that you've marked with 2, I believe we said, for the record, marks the red line that you indicated as the path that you took?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: The circle -- number 2 is inside the circle where I left. And number 3 is where Kadri Jashari was killed and where I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You have also mentioned in your statement seeing a Hermelin that day. Is the location that you saw that Hermelin in depicted in this photograph as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: The place is seen here, but -- yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you mark for us, please, with an X and an H the location of where you saw that Hermelin that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Is it marked well? X and H?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Perhaps, just for the record, the X marks the place where you saw the Hermelin that day, for the record?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we tendered this, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P217, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we show 65 ter 146, which I believe is page 2. Your Honours, I would ask that this next document not be published to the public, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the document that's before you? I believe it's displayed in both the English and Albanian languages.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If you could just take a look at the Albanian version of this document. Do you see here on the top left corner, it says "Nikustak military hospital." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And it also in bold letters in the middle says "medical discharge note." It references a name right below that, and it references a date of birth. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's correct. It's my name, my last name and my birthday.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And it also says later on, after the date of birth, it says that you were admitted to the hospital on 12 August 2001, and then it goes on, and it says "treatment for surgical treatment of the wound," and then it indicates that you were discharged on 17 September, 2001. Do you see that language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But I can't read it in English. It's my name, my birthday, resident of Ljuboten, was admitted to hospital 12 August 2001. Then I don't understand. Then I see 17 September 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, is the Albanian version before you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes. The name that I read out, I don't know how accurate I was.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: I didn't read the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, if I could just --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: The name of the doctor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, if I could just interrupt you for a second because we're in public session, and I just want to ask you, you said that the information contained -- do you see the Albanian version? And I'm asking about the Albanian version of the document, is that information contained on that document correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And you mentioned a doctor's name at the bottom. Do you see that in the very bottom left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes. Ridvan Bajrami. He's a doctor, a general practitioner in the hospital I was taken to.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And does this treatment here in the middle of the document that you've read out to us, does that treatment describe your condition -- the treatment that you received after you were wounded that day on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. What was the treatment that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: I went to Matish on Tuesday. The first treatment was given to me in Lipkov.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, my question to you was: This document indicates that you were treated -- there were surgical treatment of a wound. Is that -- is that an accurate description of what Dr. Bajrami did for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: I am not a doctor, to know my diagnosis. I believe that the doctor knows best, and I have also stated it in my statement that it wasn't possible for me to know the characteristics of my injury. I know it was in my leg up to the ankle.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: I'm not a doctor by profession.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness. Witness, my -- I guess my next question is: Did you receive this -- this paperwork from the doctor once you were released from the hospital, Nikustak hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we tender this, please, under seal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P218, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It occurs to me this is a convenient time for the break which we must have now, and we resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic has some questions now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. M-092. My name is Edina Residovic and together with my colleague, Guenael Mettraux, I appear on behalf of Mr. Ljube Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we briefly move into private session? I have a couple of questions to be dealt with that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you've stated already, you assisted in the transport of farm produce to Kosovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, we farmed the land and also transported the produce to Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The best market for your produce that you transported was in Pec and Pristina in Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes. From Strumnice to Pristina and Peja. There was a large quantity of watermelons there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Frequently, at that time, you crossed the borders between Macedonia and Kosovo, and you did so at the closest crossing point of Stenkovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: I went up to Stenkovac, but I didn't cross the border. My brother was the driver. I just helped him up to there. Then I returned home with a red Golf. My brother drove up to that point to transport the produce, but I didn't go with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you are trying to say that you, yourself, did not go to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Because it was the duty of the driver to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show to the witness a 65 ter document? The number is 1D88, page 1231, which had recently been assigned an exhibit number, P215. I would kindly ask that this document be not visible to the public, and this will also apply to several other documents that I may show to the witness during my cross-examination. Could we please show the Albanian version to the witness as well, the same page? The number is 1D1251.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In item 2, you state in the third sentence that you did not serve your military term. And then precisely as you testified, you say there that after you completed your education, you became the owner of a truck and that you exported vegetables to Pec and Pristina in Kosovo. The statement of yours, should it be viewed the way you've just explained to us, this being that you would only go as far as the border and the rest was not done by yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Stankovc.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement we have you, which in English could be understood in two different ways.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: I had licence B, but I thought I didn't pay much attention to such details, thinking that they are of no importance, but this is true. My brother has a truck even now that we are no longer working together. But at the time, we were living together and we were working together.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we are in open session, could we please have the family relation description to be redacted from line 17?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
