utterances.text: We have clarified this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think there is any need, Ms. Residovic, because there's no indication of the connection to any witness or any such matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right, Your Honours. I think this could not be put in connection with his identity from this context. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell me if it's true that you also on the 10th of August, 2001, helping transport the farming produce, that you also were in Stenkovac at the border crossing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To make the things more precise, where is that border crossing? Would it be true if I say that -- that is a border crossing which is seven to eight kilometres far away from Skopje, and that it is close to the place called Blace?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: I think that it is on the border of Hani i Elezit. It is very simple. I think that you know this already. Because Stenkovac was where all the document -- documentation of the produce and the -- and the goods is being kept, and then we went to the border point. We completed the documents. My brother went and then I came back. I think it is very clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After your answer, I think we also are a bit clearer. While going to the border crossing, you were able to note that not far away from that area, the consequences of the terrorist attacks were visible that were especially taking place towards the area of Tetovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: No, this is not true. Because there were check-points near Stenkovac, and it was not possible to do anything there. This is far away from Tetovo. And this area was -- it is -- it is very certain, whether you're a Macedonian or an Albanian, that this check-point is a Macedonian check-point and all the goods that went to Stenkovac were able to go through this check-point. But -- so this check-point was free. When you're talking about documents or other things, they were checking whether you had valid documents or about other things. I cannot tell you any further.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I was not clear in asking the question. I -- I was trying to say whether on the way to Stenkovac, you were able to see visible signs of terrorist attacks on that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: No, this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your village, Ljuboten, about which several witnesses testified before this Court, is on the hills of Skopska Crna Gore. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Ljuboten is located there together with Ljubance.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Given the geographic position of that area, it is of a special strategic importance for the city of Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: I don't know that, whether it is of a special strategic importance or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But although you don't know that, you answered my learned colleague the Prosecutor that you know that two or two and a half months before the August events, that the Army of the Republic of Macedonia was -- had deployed its forces around Ljuboten, and as you say in your statement, in your assessment, there were around 20 various check-points, whether army check-points or mixed ones?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: When I talked before, when I said that I don't know whether this was of a strategic importance, I thought probably somebody or the police, maybe they were aware of it, but I can talk only about the fact that the forces were deployed around Ljuboten, and it has been like this. This is the truth. The forces were deployed. I think they set up police check-points, and they knew -- they knew why they were doing this. But I'm not aware why did they go deep into Ljuboten two and a half months before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I completely agree with you, sir, that you're not a military expert. But as a citizen of the village of Ljuboten, you were able to confirm that you could see the entire Skopje valley from the -- most of the Ljuboten, and when the weather is sunny, you can clearly see the city of Skopje below your feet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes, Skopje is seen from that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, in front of the new newly built mosque, Skopje could be seen in a plate, as we could see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: You can see Skopje from the mosque and from the church. It is very clear, especially from the mosque you can see it better. From the church, you can see it better. But it is also seen from my house as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Maybe this personal knowledge of yours is quite important in order to assess what importance the Ljuboten position was for Skopje itself. Thank you for this clarification. But please tell me, is it true that Ljuboten was also of the interest for the NLA groups that were on -- in other areas north from Ljuboten in Matejce or in other areas? Is it correct that Ljuboten was of exceptional importance for them as well for the logistic support and its proximity to the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Well, I would treat the issue from another point of view. I told you before that people in Ljuboten were selling watermelons, and they -- they were -- they had the same thing when they were collecting tobacco, they were selling watermelon and everything they had, the farmers in Ljuboten, people who were dealing with the land, they had an agreement that people in Ljuboten will never be touched. And so that's why they did not expect that. As for what you say, those other words, I don't think they are true, because that agreement existed between Ljubance and Ljuboten, and people were free to plough their land and they -- the farmers were protecting each other, but I don't think what you're saying is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if I were to ask you whether you could confirm that quite -- quite before the Ljuboten events, groups of people have been noticed that were transporting flour or other necessities to the groups where the NLA was found, then it could be true that Ljuboten was used as a logistics base as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: I'm saying no, this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since your arrival in Ljuboten and the first NLA attacks, you had information that a number of young people from Ljuboten was joining the NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: I did not know that, but when I got the medical certificate, it is written there the date when I was wounded, the 12th. And when I was admitted into hospital on Tuesday, and two days was my travel from Ljuboten to Matejce, a shepherd met me there with his cattle, and he went there and reported. And then I was treated by Rexhep Selmani, who was the minister of health at the current government. Then I was taken from the hospital of Lipkova to Nikustak -- Nikustak. In Nikustak, I met some people who were neighbour -- inhabitants of Ljuboten, and that's it. I think this is the reality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although you met them in the centre of the 114th NLA Brigade on the 14th of August, before that you had no information that some young people from Ljuboten are joining and are fighting together with the NLA. Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: No. Only when they came to see me, I did not know what that. But during -- I saw this myself, during my treatment there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else now. Since you mentioned that it took you two days to go from Ljuboten to Matejce, you're aware that Matejce was the headquarters of the NLA Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: I knew this because of the media that there was war going on in Ljubcane [phoen]. Then they took me to Lipkov and the hospital there. They admitted me into the hospital, so I'm talking about the hospital, and I stayed there --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have already explained that. But as a person with a higher education, you surely knew that there is an old -- centuries old monastery; were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Do you mean the monastery up in the mountain? Can you explain it a bit clearer?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Matejce monastery, which was under the auspices of UNESCO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And while being in that area you were surely able to see that the monastery was -- was totally demolished by the -- and devastated by the NLA groups and that it was desecrated. Have you -- do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: I visited the monastery later after I recovered from my wounds. If you want to make a comparison, probably I've seen any sign later, but if you want to compare, as I mentioned it before, also the church and the mosque are unique in their religion, and I don't know, probably there were more mosques that were demolished in comparison to the churches, because there are young people who can get out of control, but I don't think it was demolished to that extent. This is what I'm talking about, what I'm saying -- what I saw with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, are we working until 7.00?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you know Islam Zendeli? But if are you related to him, please don't mention the relationship.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Zendeli Islam was one of those, who was among the first ones from the village of Ljuboten, who joined the NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: I learned this because at the time he had a house in Topansko and when I was admitted to the hospital, I learned that he was working somewhere, he's dealing with something, and I did not know what he was doing. It was there that I learned that he was there (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask to redact the relationship.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If Islam Zendeli, in his statement given to the Prosecutor of the ICTY, were to claim that at that time there were between 25 and 27 persons from Ljuboten who were active NLA fighters, then you would agree that that fact would be a correct one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: No, I do not know that. I've only saw those people who visited me there. I do not know this, how many people were there from Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ljuboten is not a big place, and there are big families there, and the facts of that nature have surely been known to the inhabitants of Ljuboten. Tell me, is it true that given your business, you were -- you had no knowledge that such a -- such a large number of young men from Ljuboten had joined the NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: I think so, because I do not know this. I don't know this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please move into a private session for a while?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have stated that you left your brother and your truck at the border crossing, and you returned to Skopje with your car; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes. But in Skopje we left the car there, and then I -- as far as I can remember, we took -- we headed for Radishan then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you say that you left the car in Skopje, you left the car at the area of Skopje that is called Bit Pazar; is that correct? You took bus number 57, and you came to Radishan; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: Yes. It's 57. It's 57.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: And the bus bears this number even today.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your vehicle on the way from Stenkovac to Skopje, were you alone and you -- you were alone and you went to Radishan alone; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-092
utterances.text: No. Up to -- up to Skopje, I went -- I was by myself and then I waited for Isa there because he said, Wait for me because I will go and see my family. And then I waited at the Bit Pazar. This is all I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Have you something that you want to say, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I do have some information for the Chamber. Perhaps the witness could be escorted out first, and then I have some information to provide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We must adjourn now for the evening. We resume tomorrow at 2.15, and we would ask you to return then. The court officer will show you out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we move into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We now adjourn for the evening, and we resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 23rd day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.,
